items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: And McKinley Thomas and Baritone, we had a band around there, including the singing brothers, Homer and Al Simeon.

ctx.x: Well, what about before you went to school? Did you hear any music?

Yeah. Well, sometime my mother would have a fish fry and she was engaged with Roy Palmer. He had a friend that played a mountain. Later on you know Roy Palmer played baritone, cornet, trombone, a lot of instruments. He was a pretty good teacher. He taught a lot of people around Chicago, including myself and Lionel Hampton and Oscar Bunny Young, who I later played with at the Wisconsin Roof for about six years. And McKinley Thomas and Baritone, we had a band around there, including the singing brothers, Homer and…

Where was Eddie Atkinson from? New Orleans. I never heard of him down here. Oh, I've seen his greatest, he's buried out by Ron Wagamahema. Did he play with bass down here? Yeah, I think so, but not in early years. In early years.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: And so then I, then they formed a band. There's two Simeon brothers which is from New Orleans. Yeah. And there was Jimmy Mackenzie on the drum, myself and Bernie and sometimes Dominic.

ctx.x: But how old were you about when you started playing jobs in around Chicago?

Oh I started playing about, I was playing pretty good in eight months. You were about 19 or something like that? I always did get a fair tone you know. It was a Mexican show, just a solid tone. Yeah. And so then I, then they formed a band. There's two Simeon brothers which is from New Orleans. Yeah. And there was Jimmy Mackenzie on the drum, myself and Bernie and sometimes Dominic. And so Richard Jones on piano, one time he had the band.
So you started working pretty fast after you.

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Then I met Simeon boys. Oh yeah. Al Simeon and Omar Simeon... So Bernie got these fellas together and we formed a little band.

ctx.x: So when was the first music that you were interested in? Did you start on the trombone or which instrument did you start on?

Well, my first instrument was trombone, but it wasn't my favorite instrument. I'd like to tell you, Bill, about how I come to study the trombone. While talking with Joe Oliver, it must have been somewhere around 1920, 1921, somewhere along there. He, I told Joe Oliver that I was going to take lessons on the trombone. So he says, why don't you try the clarinet? The reason Joe suggested to me to take the, take up the clarinet was because I used to whistle so good. And he said people did. So he thought if a fella…
